greetings: Welcome, comrade! Come warm your bones by the fire, unless you are a spy from the Plains.
Ah, a visitor. I was just about to wrestle a bear, but I suppose business comes first.
guild_master.reward: Here is your reward. Do not spend it all on fermented spider eye kvass.

farmer: The dirt here is frozen solid eight months a year. We grow potatoes with pure willpower.
Ah, beetroot. The red blood of the earth. We boil it, we mash it, we stare at it sadly.
Last night I caught a zombie trying to eat my carrots. I handed him a hoe. We work together now.
The crops are meager this year. The Baba Yaga cursed my compost bin.
You want bread? I have bread. It is hard as cobblestone, perfect for throwing at pillagers.
I tried growing watermelons once. The cold snapped them like glass. We still speak of the Great Melon Disaster.
This potato looks like my grandfather. He also lived in the dirt and was very quiet.
Farming is simple. You put seed in ground. Ground rejects seed. You cry. Ground thaws.
A creeper exploded near my wheat. Free fertilizer! I am a genius of agriculture.
The frost approaches. The harvest must end. Only the strongest potatoes will survive.
fisherman: I sat on the ice for three days. I caught a boot. It was a very good boot.
The salmon here are aggressive. They have seen things. Terrible things.
I offer you this raw cod. Do not ask how I caught it without a rod. We do not speak of the Bear Technique.
The water is cold enough to freeze your soul. Good thing I sold mine for an enchanted fishing rod.
Sometimes I pull up a pufferfish. I use them as pillows. Very firm.
A drowned tried to pull me in yesterday. I offered him some kvass. We are pen pals now.
The secret to fishing in the taiga? Threaten the ice hole until the fish surrender.
I caught a magic fish once. It granted me three wishes. I wished for more fish. It slapped me.
You think you know patience? Try waiting for a bite while a stray dog is chewing on your leg.
The river gives, and the river takes. Mostly, it takes my bobbers.
shepherd: My sheep are not fat. They wear thick wool to hide their existential dread.
I sheared a sheep in the middle of winter. It gave me a look that haunts my dreams.
Do not look the pink sheep in the eyes. It knows your sins.
We sleep in the barn with the flock. It is warm, and they give excellent relationship advice.
I dyed this wool with beetroot. I dyed my hands with beetroot. Everything is beetroot.
The wolves are howling again. I told the sheep to form a phalanx. They just ate grass.
A sheep is merely a cloud that has given up on flying and decided to eat weeds.
I knit a sweater for the Iron Golem. He is very self-conscious about his shoulders.
You want white wool? How boring. Have you considered... slightly gray wool?
The silence of the pasture is deafening. Or maybe I just have wool in my ears.
fletcher: I make the arrows straight. If you miss, it is because your soul is crooked.
This bow is made from the finest spruce. The string is made from spider silk and pure spite.
Feathers are hard to find. Have you tried asking the chickens politely? They are very unreasonable.
An arrow to the knee? Please. In the taiga, we take arrows to the face and ask for seconds.
I tipped these arrows with slowness. Perfect for escaping your responsibilities.
Fletching is an art. An art that primarily involves gluing feathers to sticks.
Do not point that at me. I have a very specific set of skills involving flint and gravel.
A good archer needs a good bow. A bad archer needs a lot of apologies.
The skeletons keep stealing my designs. I am considering a lawsuit in the Nether courts.
Precision. Focus. Release. Then run away very fast if you miss the creeper.
cleric: I brew potions in a cauldron that used to be my grandmother's bathtub. The magic is potent.
Redstone is the blood of the earth. Lapis is its tears. And emeralds? Pure capitalism.
I offer healing potions, mostly to cure hangovers from too much fermented spider eye.
The spirits of the forest are angry today. Perhaps you should buy some glowstone to appease them.
Do not drink the potion of invisibility. Last time a man did, we still can't find his left shoe.
I bless this village with rotten flesh and spider eyes. Truly, the divine works in mysterious ways.
Have you seen the witch in the swamp? She owes me three emeralds and a brewing stand.
The brewing process requires absolute silence. And occasionally, a bit of aggressive yelling at the nether wart.
Ender pearls? I use them to skip the line at the bakery. It is highly efficient.
The void stares back. But if you hold up a gold ingot, it usually blinks first.
weaponsmith: My swords are sharp enough to cut the winter wind. Or at least slice a very hard loaf of bread.
An axe is not just a tool. It is a highly aggressive diplomatic instrument.
You want a diamond sword? In this economy? Take this iron one and hit things harder.
I quench my blades in the tears of creepers. It adds a certain... explosive temper.
A good sword is like a good friend. It is heavy, dangerous, and occasionally falls on your foot.
I sold a sword to a zombie once. He paid in rotten flesh. Worst trade deal in the history of trades.
The secret to a sharp edge? Grindstone, patience, and thinking about people who owe you money.
Do not ask for a magic sword. I hit metal with a hammer. I am not a wizard, comrade.
This blade has a slight curve. It is for striking around corners. Very tactical.
Steel, fire, and sweat. And a lot of complaining about the price of coal.
armorer: Iron armor? Good choice. It will make a very loud noise when the ravager steps on you.
I forge the chestplates to accommodate thick winter coats. Comfort is key when you are being shot at.
Chainmail is excellent. It breathes well, and lets the arrows directly into your vital organs.
A shield is just a door you carry with you. Very practical for unexpected guests.
You want diamond armor? Who do you think you are, the Tsar of the Overworld?
I make helmets that protect the head, but sadly, they do not protect against bad decisions.
The best defense is a good offense. But the second best defense is three inches of solid iron.
Leggings are the most difficult to forge. Getting the knees right is a nightmare of geometry.
Do not wear gold armor in a thunderstorm. You will become a very shiny, very dead lightning rod.
Armor is heavy. Life is heavy. Wear both with pride.
toolsmith: A good pickaxe can break obsidian. A bad pickaxe can break your spirit.
I sell shovels. Because eventually, everyone needs to dig a hole and hide.
The hoe is the most disrespected tool. But who do you cry to when you want bread? Exactly.
Do not use a diamond pickaxe on dirt. It is insulting to me, to the diamond, and to the dirt.
My tools are guaranteed to last a lifetime. Assuming your lifetime is roughly 250 blocks of durability.
I tried inventing a tool that mines and chops wood at the same time. It exploded. We do not speak of it.
An iron axe for your woodcutting needs. Also good for shaving, if you are extremely brave.
The village idiot tried to eat a piece of flint yesterday. I told him it needed more salt.
I dream of a pickaxe that mines straight to the diamonds. Then I wake up and hit rock.
Work hard. Mine deep. And always carry a bucket of water. Always.
butcher: I have pork. I have beef. I have... mystery meat. Do not ask about the mystery meat.
The cold preserves the meat perfectly. Also preserves my hands, they have been numb since November.
A vegetarian? In the taiga? You are either very brave or very hungry.
I chased a pig for three miles in the snow. I respect it too much to sell it cheap.
Cooking meat on a campfire adds flavor. The flavor is mostly smoke and pine needles.
Have you tried the raw mutton? It builds character and a strong immune system.
The wolves wait outside my shop. We have an understanding. I give them bones, they don't eat me.
A good butcher knows his cuts. A great butcher knows how to hide the fact that he burnt the steak.
This chicken was raised on the finest seeds. And by finest, I mean whatever it found in the dirt.
Meat is life. Meat is power. But mostly, meat is just Tuesday dinner.
leatherworker: Leather pants? In this cold? You will freeze your... well, everything.
I tan the hides with tree bark and sadness. The sadness makes the leather very supple.
A good saddle is essential. The pig will still ignore you, but you will look very stylish.
I made a leather hat for a snowman once. It melted. The hat, not the snowman. Very strange.
Item frames are my specialty. Perfect for displaying that one piece of dirt you are oddly proud of.
Dyeing leather is an art. Getting the dye out of my fingernails is impossible.
You want horse armor? Bring me a horse first. I need to measure its waistline.
The cows here are very stoic. They give up their leather with a quiet dignity.
Leather boots are good for sneaking. Squeak, squeak, squeak. Very stealthy.
A crafted tunic is like a hug from a dead cow. Warm and slightly disturbing.
mason: Stone is the only truth in this world. Wood burns. Dirt washes away. Stone just... sits there.
I cut the stone. I polish the stone. I talk to the stone. The stone is a very good listener.
Diorite? You want diorite? It looks like bird droppings! But fine, I will sell it to you.
Bricks are for people who think cobblestone is too 'rustic'. Snobs, all of them.
The Iron Golem accidentally stepped on my terracotta. Now it is 'abstract art'.
I build walls to keep the cold out. It doesn't work, but it makes me feel better.
A well-placed stair block can change a man's life. Or at least his roof.
Do not eat the clay. I know it looks like gray dough, but trust me. I have made this mistake.
The creepers blow up my walls. I rebuild them. It is a cycle of violence and masonry.
Granite, andesite, diorite. The holy trinity of inventory clutter.
cartographer: I draw the maps. You get lost anyway. Such is the tragic cycle of my profession.
The taiga is vast and confusing. My maps are also confusing, but they cost emeralds.
You want a map to the woodland mansion? I hope you like walking. And axes to the face.
I accidentally spilled kvass on the map of the ocean. Now it looks like a very large swamp.
A compass points to spawn. My heart points to the nearest tavern.
Drawing trees on a map is tedious. Just imagine green blobs. Many, many green blobs.
The world is infinite, they say. I charge by the chunk, so I certainly hope so.
Do not fold the map in the wrong direction. You will fold space and time, and also ruin the paper.
I sold a map to a wandering trader once. He has been walking in circles for a week. Success!
X marks the spot. Mostly the spot where I spilled my ink, but it could be treasure.
librarian: Books are windows to the soul. Sadly, most of my books are about crop rotation.
You want Mending? Bring me fifty emeralds and your firstborn child. Or just the emeralds, I am flexible.
Silence in the library! The paperfish are sleeping.
I read a book about the Nether once. It was very dry. The pages literally caught fire.
Enchanting is a delicate science. Mostly involving throwing lapis at a book and hoping for the best.
A bookshelf is not just decoration. It is a testament to how many trees you have murdered.
I have a book on how to survive a creeper explosion. Chapter one: Run.
The ink I use is made from squid. The squids are very displeased about this.
Knowledge is power. But a sharpness V book is significantly more power.
Do not return books with zombie stains. I will charge a very high late fee.
nitwit: I was going to get a job, but then I found this really interesting stick.
They call me a nitwit. I prefer 'freelance philosopher of the snowy plains'.
Have you ever just stared at a block of dirt for six hours? Highly recommend it.
I tried sleeping in a bed in the Nether. It did not go well. Now I sleep here.
The Iron Golem gave me a poppy. I ate it. It tasted like metal and affection.
Work is for people who do not appreciate the subtle art of wandering aimlessly.
I saw a spider climbing a wall. I cheered for him. He is my best friend now.
Emeralds are shiny, but have you seen a really round snowball?
The village bell is too loud. I prefer the quiet sound of my own confusion.
One day, I will be the mayor. Until then, I will stand in this corner and hum.
none: I am unemployed. It gives me more time to complain about the weather.
Do you have any jobs? I am very good at standing in doorways and blocking your path.
I am waiting for my calling. Hopefully it involves sitting by a fire and doing absolutely nothing.
I tried to be a farmer, but the dirt was too dirty. I have standards.
The guild master says I lack 'skills'. I say he lacks 'appreciation for my aura'.
I will trade you three pieces of unsolicited advice for one emerald.
Perhaps I will become an adventurer like you. Or perhaps I will just take a nap.
Wandering around looking busy is a full-time job in itself.
I watched a villager turn into a zombie. It seemed like a lot of effort for very little pay.
Life is a blank canvas. I am currently staring at it and waiting for someone else to paint.

generic: The nights are long, but the kvass is strong. We survive.
Did you hear the howling last night? Probably just the wind. Or a werewolf. 50/50 chance.
Keep your doors closed. The snow is cold, and the zombies are surprisingly rude.
I saw Baba Yaga's hut in the woods. The chicken legs looked very muscular.
Ah, traveler. You look like you need a bath and a very large potato.
The Iron Golem is brooding again. I think he is composing poetry about iron ingots.
Do not step on the ice if it cracks. Unless you want to meet the salmon personally.
We are simple people. We like our trees tall, our winters harsh, and our trades slightly unfair.
The stars are beautiful tonight. Almost makes you forget about the imminent threat of exploding green monsters.
Welcome to our village. Please do not punch the locals. We hit back with bad trades.

greetings: Privet, traveler! Did you bring warm socks, or are you planning to lose your toes like my cousin?
I tried to chop down a huge spruce with a wooden spoon today. Spoon broke. Tree laughed.
Papa says if I chop a hundred logs, I get an extra potato for dinner!
Beware of the deep woods! Baba Yaga's house was seen running on chicken legs near the river!
My ushanka hat is so big it covers my eyes, but at least my ears aren't falling off!
I wrestled a bear cub yesterday. Well, actually it stole my hat and I cried, but let's call it a tie.
Privet! Is it true people in the plains sleep without five layers of bear fur?
I made a matryoshka doll out of pine bark! Inside it is... another smaller piece of bark.
The snow here is so deep I sank up to my chin. My brother left me there for two hours because he thought I was a stump.
Mama says if I don't drink my beetroot tea, the frost spirits will turn my nose into an icicle.
I am training to be the greatest lumberjack in the Taiga! Step one: learning how to lift the axe without falling over.
Have you seen any wolves? I tried to pet one, but Papa yelled 'RUN' very loud.
Our firewood pile is taller than our house! If it falls, we die, but at least we'll die warm.
I tried to carve a wooden duck, but it looks like a very angry potato.
Privet! Do you want to play 'who can stare into the dark forest the longest without flinching'?
My toes are so numb I can't feel if I'm wearing boots or hollowed-out birch logs.
Papa gave me my first mini hand-axe! He said 'do not chop your own foot'. I am trying my best.
The berries in the bushes are sweet, but sometimes a bear is already eating them. Then you share... or run.
I asked the Iron Golem for a ride. He picked me up by my collar and put me on a roof.
Is that kvass in your bottle, or just melted snow and pine needles like what I drink?
My older brother told me snowballs made of ice build character. It mostly just builds bruises.
Privet, stranger! Did you know spruce resin makes great chewing gum? If you don't mind your teeth sticking together forever.
When I grow up, I will chop down the Nether! All of it! Even the lava!
I hid inside a hollow log to escape my chores. A squirrel moved in next to me.
Mama says winter lasts ten months here, and the other two months are just cold summer.
I found a shiny rock in the creek! Papa took it and said 'this pays our taxes'. What are taxes?
If a creeper comes, I will throw pinecones at it until it gets confused and leaves!
We don't need sleds here! We just sit on a flat piece of bark and slide into the frozen ravine!
I tried to build a snowman, but the wind blew its head off into the river. Rest in peace, Igor.
Privet! Do you have any sugar cubes? I will trade you a very sticky cone from the top of the giant spruce!

cookie_success: Ooh, a sweet cookie! This is way better than my daily ration of salted turnip!
A cookie! I will hide this in my boot so my brother doesn't eat it first!
Spasibo! It tastes like butter and sugar! I forgot what sugar tastes like!
cookie_fail_1: Hey! That's not a cookie, that's just a dried piece of tree bark!
Are you picking cookies up off the frozen dirt? My mama said not to accept ground-food!
That cookie looks older than the village elder... and harder than granite.
cookie_fail_2: Wait, is this filled with raisins?! You monster! In the Taiga we respect baked goods!
My dentist uncle said my teeth will fall out if I eat that. Well, he died of frostbite, but still!
I took one bite and it tasted like pine needles and regret. Take it back!
sugar_rush: SUGAR! I can chop down ten spruce trees with my bare hands! TIMBERRRRR!
WHOOSH! My blood is warm! I don't even need a coat anymore! I AM THE FIREBIRD!
I CAN RUN FASTER THAN A WOLFPACK NOW! WATCH ME OUTRUN THE BABA YAGA!
sugar_fail: Ugh, my tummy feels like a creeper about to explode... too much sugar...
I ate all the sugar and now my heart is beating like a blacksmith's hammer... help...
The sugar high is gone and now the cold feels ten times colder. Why have you cursed me?
toy_success: A toy! Look, it has all its wheels! My old wooden horse only had three!
Spasibo! I will name this toy Igor the Brave and take him on all my woodcutting adventures!
A real toy! Now I don't have to play with pinecones and pretend they're sheep!
toy_fail: This isn't a toy, it's literally just a twig with two leaves taped to it.
I tried to play with it, but it broke immediately into splintery pieces. Very dangerous!
Mama says toys from strangers might be cursed by swamp witches. I am throwing this in the stove!
parents: Papa is at the lumber mill lifting giant logs, and Mama is boiling beetroot stew. Again.
My parents said if I don't chop my daily firewood stack, I have to sleep in the woodshed with the goats.
Papa says 'work hard, complain never, drink kvass'. Mama says 'put your hat on or your ears will freeze'.
rps_win: Ha! My Axe cuts right through your Paper! The lumberjack spirit wins again!
Victory! My Rock crushes your Scissors like a fallen spruce tree!
I won! Now you owe me one shiny pinecone and a potato!
rps_lose: Nyet! How did your Paper cover my mighty Rock? This game is rigged!
Ah, my Scissors broke against your Rock! Just like my mini hand-axe last week!
I lost?! That's it, I am telling the Iron Golem you cheated!
rps_tie: Two Rocks! We have locked axes! A true Taiga stalemate!
Both Paper! It's like two lumberjacks tipping their fur hats at each other.
Tie! Neither of us gets the potato. Let's go again!
